arm-01.note: domain/legacy-import.ts: dedupes customers via legacySourceId/email/phone, mints a fresh sequential orderNumber per season for every imported order (the source's own orderNumber field is optional and is NOT preserved as the app's order number, only implicitly traceable via legacySourceId), 4-stage resumable commit (catalog->customers->addresses->orders).

arm-03.note: lib/ops/import.ts classifyOrderRows(): explicit repair for blank/invalid order numbers (minted from an 800000+i range when unrepairable), resumable staged commit with a cursor for customer/product/order kinds.

arm-04.note: lib/migration/legacy-rows.ts repairOrderReference() + lib/migration/legacy-commit.ts: repairs malformed legacy order numbers where a fix can be derived and otherwise flags the row as a problem for review, but ALWAYS preserves the true historical reference (importedOrderReference) rather than discarding it for a freshly-minted number — orders stay keyed by their real legacy identity; resumable chunked commit.

arm-05.note: No Nexternal/legacy-order concept exists anywhere in the tree (verified via grep for 'legacy'/'nexternal'/'legacyRef' — zero matches). app/api/admin/imports/route.ts + lib/admin-operations.ts only stage/commit simple customer or product CSV rows (email/phone/name, or sku/name/price) with no order-number repair, no historical order ingestion, no season creation from imports. This is a fundamentally different, much smaller feature than the legacy migration pipeline the item asks for.

arm-06.note: lib/imports/legacy/{orders,customers,products,seasons,resolve-customer}.ts: order-number repair is unconditional (claimOrderNumber() mints a fresh per-season sequential number for every imported order while preserving the old system's number verbatim on Order.legacyRef), unmapped products land as inactive $0 stubs feeding the repeat-order review flow, batched customer-match lookups avoid N+1 inside the commit transaction. At least as thorough as the clone cluster.

arm-01.note: app/api/health/route.ts: SELECT 1 DB check, returns auth mode; env validation is implicit — importing lib/db transitively calls readServerEnvironment(), which throws at import time only if DATABASE_URL is missing (no other provider vars are validated).

arm-03.note: app/api/health/route.ts explicitly calls getEnv() INSIDE the handler on every request (not just relying on module-load-time validation as a side effect), plus the SELECT 1 DB check — the most request-time-explicit env-validation story of the three.

arm-04.note: app/api/health/route.ts imports the eagerly-validated `env` singleton and documents the intent directly at the call site ('Green means the process booted with valid env AND can reach Postgres. A reachable app with a dead database must not report healthy.'), plus the DB check; also carefully masks Postgres connection-string details from the response body.

arm-05.note: app/api/health/route.ts: DB connectivity check only (SELECT 1); lib/env.ts is barely used elsewhere (only Clerk keys) so there's effectively no env-validation story surfaced through health at all.

arm-06.note: app/api/health/route.ts explicitly imports '@/lib/env' as a documented side-effect ('validates env at boot; a bad value crashes startup with a clear message before this route ever serves') plus the DB check — same underlying mechanism as the clone cluster but the intent is deliberately called out at the health-route call site rather than left implicit.
